heroSub: 10 hand-picked budget Uthai Thani stays we've reviewed, all scoring 8.1+ — from a garden bungalow resort at ฿650 and the only pool resort in the guide to an old-town wood-house guesthouse and riverside homestays on the Sakae Krang. From roughly ฿650–1,200/night, ranked by value.
introH2: 💰 Can you do Uthai Thani on a budget — and which area is best value?
introHtml: Uthai Thani is a small, underrated town on the Sakae Krang river where rooms are still genuinely cheap — well-reviewed stays scoring in the high 8s to low 9s start in the ฿600s to low ฿1,000s, spanning garden bungalows, a pool resort, old-town wood-house guesthouses and riverside homestays. The key to doing Uthai Thani on a budget is to match the area to your plans, because the sights are spread out and your location decides whether you need a car. The old town centre (Uthai Mai) is walkable to the riverside morning market, the Trok Rong Ya walking street and local restaurants — ideal without a car. The Sakae Krang riverside and Koh Thepho suit those who want to sleep by the water and cycle, but most need a car and a drive across the bridge into town. And the suburbs toward Ban Rai (Tha Pho, Thap Than, Highway 333) suit drivers who want a pool resort or a quiet garden stay for less. The trick to real value is not to pick on price alone — weigh whether you have a car, whether you want a pool, and check the review count, because some of the cheapest stays are suburban and mean driving into town for every meal. This guide rounds up 10 budget Uthai Thani stays we've already reviewed, all scoring 8.1+, from roughly ฿650–1,200/night, with real guest-review scores, a 3-site price comparison and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Uthai Thani has no metro, and it's a small, flat town you can explore on foot or by bike — but the sights are spread out enough that your choice of area sets up the whole trip, and decides whether you need a car. Many old-town (Uthai Mai) stays are walkable to the Sakae Krang riverside morning market, the Trok Rong Ya walking street and local restaurants, ideal without a car (Comenietee Uthai · Sabua The Terrace · TJ Boutique). Stays on the Sakae Krang riverside and Koh Thepho mostly need a car, about a 10-minute drive across the bridge into town, but reward you with riverside atmosphere and the popular Koh Thepho cycling loop (Sakaekrang Haven · Ban Klang Gaew). And almost everything in the suburbs toward Ban Rai (Tha Pho, Thap Than, Nong Kae, Highway 333) needs a private car, as there's little to walk to nearby (Numhom · Uthaithani · C2U · S Ville). Many people book a cheap suburban stay expecting to walk to the morning market, then end up driving into town for every meal — so check the location before you book.

entries.name: Numhom Resort
entries.revCount: Agoda 9.1 · 167 reviews · cheapest in this guide ฿650
entries.badge: 🏆 Best value in this guide · from ฿650
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Thap Than · between town & Ban Rai · ~20-min drive to town
entries.addr: 4/2 Moo 6, Thap Than, Thap Than District, Uthai Thani
entries.storyHtml: Numhom Resort is the best value in this guide — the cheapest at ฿650 yet scoring 9.1 from 167 reviews, a garden-bungalow resort in Thap Than that suits families and drivers heading out toward Ban Rai. It sits midway between the town and Ban Rai district, right on the route. Real guest reviews praise the clean, roomy, private rooms, bungalows facing a small pond, a kids' playground and broad garden for children to run around, and warm staff. The trade-off: it's in Thap Than, about a 20-minute drive into town each time you want the market or the Sakae Krang riverside, and the resort hosts functions and karaoke, so it can get noisy when there's an event. Best for families and drivers exploring the west of the province.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pick a bungalow facing the pond for the full effect; travelling in a group, look at the four-bed family room. If you want total quiet, ask the resort whether there's a function or karaoke on your dates, and choose a bungalow far from the event area.

Kids' playground and broad garden, great for families
Midway between town and Ban Rai, easy access to the west
On-site restaurant, BBQ corner, free parking at your door
cons: In Thap Than — about a 20-minute drive into town

entries.name: Uthaithani Resort
entries.badge: 🏊 The only pool in this guide · ฿850
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Tha Pho, Nong Khayang · on a main road · ~10-min drive to town
tags: 🌿 Pretty garden, faux waterfall, photo spots
🚗 Easy to find on a main road · EV charger
entries.addr: 111 Moo 2, Tha Pho, Nong Khayang District, Uthai Thani
entries.storyHtml: Uthaithani Resort is a two-storey wooden resort with separate adult and kids' pools — the only pool in this budget guide, scoring 8.7 from 120 reviews, from just ฿850. Most stays in town are small boutiques without a pool, but this is a fuller resort, with a landscaped garden, faux waterfall and several photo spots. Real guest reviews praise clean, nicely sized rooms, the pretty garden, a pool the kids love, helpful owner and staff, and an EV charging point. The catch: it's in suburban Tha Pho, so you drive into town for every meal, and it gets busy on long weekends. Best for families with children and groups who like to take photos.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pick a pool-view or garden-view room for the full effect; travelling in a group, look at the three-bed room. Driving yourself is easiest since you'll head into town to eat and explore. It's popular with families on long weekends, so book ahead.
pros: Separate adult and kids' pools — the only pool in this budget guide
Pretty garden, faux waterfall, lots of photo spots · clean rooms
Easy to find on a main road · EV charging point
On-site restaurant + cafe · free parking
cons: In suburban Tha Pho — you drive into town to eat and explore

entries.name: S Ville Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Uthai Mai · near Khao Sakae Krang · ~10-min drive to town
tags: 🛏️ Bigger rooms than the price, with a bathtub
⛰️ Near Khao Sakae Krang for city views
entries.addr: 295 Moo 3, Nam Suem, Mueang Uthai Thani
entries.storyHtml: S Ville Resort is a small ~11-room resort in the Uthai Mai area that guests love for rooms bigger than the price and the quiet, scoring 8.2 from 19 reviews. It's near Khao Sakae Krang, the city's viewpoint hill, about a 10-minute drive into the centre. Real guest reviews praise rooms larger than expected and easy to move around in, comfy beds, clean bedding, and bathtubs in several bathrooms, plus a quiet, leafy garden and free, generous parking. The point reviewers raise most is that the entrance is hard to find and the access lane is a bit isolated, it's a small resort with no pool, and there's nothing to walk to nearby. Best for drivers who want a big, quiet room on a budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Call ahead for directions or exact coordinates before you set off, as the entrance is hard to find, especially after dark. If you like a soak, request a room with a bathtub when booking. Use the resort as a base to drive up Khao Sakae Krang for merit-making and city views in the morning.
pros: Rooms bigger than the price, with a bathtub, comfy beds
Small, quiet, leafy garden resort, private
Near Khao Sakae Krang for city views
Free, generous parking, great for drivers
cons: Hard-to-find entrance, somewhat isolated lane; call ahead
Small resort, no pool · nothing walkable nearby

entries.name: C2U Hotel Uthai Thani
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Out of town · Highway 333 · Nong Kae · ~5 km from town

entries.addr: 88 Moo 1, Nong Kae, Mueang Uthai Thani (on Highway 333)
entries.storyHtml: C2U Hotel Uthai Thani is a newly opened out-of-town hotel with the most reviews in this guide — 828 reviews, scoring 8.1 — whose selling point is clean, modern rooms with good beds at a low price. It's a 3-storey, ~36-room hotel on the bypass road (Highway 333) in Nong Kae, about 5 km from town. Real guest reviews agree the rooms are very clean, with comfy beds, quality bedding and well-placed bedside outlets, plus a continental breakfast, a minimart and a 24-hour front desk. But it's out of town with nothing walkable nearby, so you drive in for every meal, there's no pool, and at times it takes cash only. Best for drivers who want a good room and easy parking.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: This suits people with a car — plan lunch and dinner in town since there's nothing around the hotel, about a 10-minute drive. Bring some cash and check the payment terms in advance. Arriving late is fine; there's a 24-hour front desk.
pros: Most reviews in the guide (828) · very clean new rooms, good beds
Free generous parking, easy in and out, great for drivers
Continental breakfast · minimart · 24-hour desk
From about ฿800/night, great value for a good room

entries.name: Ban Klang Gaew Resort
entries.badge: 🚲 Riverside on Koh Thepho · cycling base
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Koh Thepho · on the Sakae Krang · ~10–15-min drive over the bridge
tags: 🏡 Standalone cabins with balconies, lovely owner
entries.addr: 36 Moo 5, Koh Thepho, Mueang Uthai Thani
entries.storyHtml: Ban Klang Gaew Resort (Baan Klang Ko) is a riverside stay on Koh Thepho with the most reviews among the resorts in this guide — 186 reviews, scoring 8.7 — and the most natural cycling base for the island. Koh Thepho is a popular cycling loop full of rice fields, pomelo orchards and riverside temples. Real guest reviews praise the quiet riverside atmosphere, standalone cabins with sit-out balconies, cleanliness, and a warm, attentive owner. But it's on the island, so you need a car and a 10–15-minute drive across the bridge into town, there's nothing to walk to nearby, and there's no pool or breakfast included. Best for nature lovers and cyclists.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Bring your own bike or ask about rentals, and ride around Koh Thepho in the morning starting from Wat Uposatharam. There are no restaurants nearby, so plan meals in town, a 10–15-minute drive over the bridge. Book ahead in the cool season and on long weekends, when cyclists flock here.
pros: Most reviews among the resorts (186) · quiet riverside feel
Cycling base around Koh Thepho amid rice fields & pomelo orchards
Standalone cabins with balconies, green garden, caring owner
Free parking, great for drivers
cons: On the island; needs a car, drive over the bridge, nothing walkable nearby
No pool · breakfast mostly not included

entries.name: Comenietee Uthai
entries.badge: 🪵 Old-town wood house · walk to market
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Old town, Uthai Mai · 200 m walk to the morning market
tags: 🚶 200 m to the riverside morning market

entries.addr: 43/11-12 Phon Phibun Uthit Rd, Uthai Mai, Mueang Uthai Thani
entries.storyHtml: Comenietee Uthai is a guesthouse in a renovated old Thai wood house right in the old town, scoring a high 9.0 on Booking — a warm wooden-home feel where you can walk everywhere. It has just 4 rooms, about a 200-metre walk to the Sakae Krang riverside morning market, beside the old-town square with cafes, bars and local restaurants. Real guest reviews praise comfy beds, cool air-con, strong WiFi, a friendly owner who runs it personally, and a generous Thai breakfast. But with only 4 rooms you must book ahead, some rooms have a private bathroom out on the balcony (not in-room), so check the room type first, and there's no pool. Best for soaking up old-town Uthai Thani up close.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you want a proper in-room bathroom, pick a Superior or large-bed room and confirm with the property. With only 4 rooms, always book ahead, especially on long weekends. Head out early for the riverside morning market just steps away.
pros: Booking 9.0 · warm renovated wood house in the old town
200 m to the riverside morning market, beside the old-town square
Owner-run · generous Thai breakfast
Free parking, rare in the narrow-lane old town
cons: Only 4 rooms, fills fast on long weekends · some bathrooms are out of the room
No pool · small place with few reviews so far

entries.name: Shon Boutique
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Soi Na Thong · town · near the provincial court · quiet off-lane
tags: 🌿 Newly opened, English Garden style, garden
🛏️ Clean rooms, strong hot water, smart TV
entries.addr: 8/128 Soi Na Thong, Uthai Sai Rd, Uthai Mai, Mueang Uthai Thani
entries.storyHtml: Shon Boutique is a newly opened in-town boutique in an English-garden style, whose draw is its newness, quiet, and being pet-friendly — rare in Uthai Thani town, scoring about 8.5–8.6 from its first reviews. It sits in Soi Na Thong near the provincial court, tucked off the lane so it's quiet, a few minutes' drive to the morning market and Trok Rong Ya. Real guest reviews praise clean, new-looking rooms, strong hot water, comfy beds, friendly staff, a garden to relax in, and a buffet breakfast. But standard rooms are fairly compact with little storage, it's new so reviews are still few, and there's no full restaurant on site. Best for a new, quiet, garden stay, or if you're travelling with a pet.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Travelling in a group with big bags? Request the family room when you book, as standard rooms are compact. Bringing a pet, message their page or call to confirm first. As a new property, message the page about promotions — some periods start at ฿900 with breakfast.

Quiet and private, with an English Garden
Pet-friendly, rare in town · on-site parking

cons: Standard rooms fairly compact with little storage

entries.name: Sabua The Terrace Homestay
entries.badge: 🪷 Lotus-pond garden home · walk to walking street
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Soi Suk Kasem · town centre · walk to Trok Rong Ya walking street
tags: 🪷 Old lotus pond with a boardwalk out front
🚶 Shortcut to the walking street & morning market
entries.addr: 8 Soi Suk Kasem, Uthai Mai, Mueang Uthai Thani
entries.storyHtml: Sabua The Terrace Homestay is a garden home in the town centre with consistently high review scores around 9 — its signatures are a big old lotus pond out front and a location you can walk everywhere from. A shortcut through the pond gets you to the Trok Rong Ya walking street and the Sakae Krang riverside morning market in minutes, no car needed. Real guest reviews praise a kind owner who shares tips, spotless rooms, air-conditioned rooms with balconies overlooking the lotus pond, and breakfast included. It is a small homestay, though — only a few rooms, no 24-hour staff (you sometimes arrange check-in time with the owner), and no pool. Best for staying in the centre with a garden-home feel while still walking to everything.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Take in the lotus blooms from the balcony in the morning, then cut through the pond for rice soup at the riverside morning market. It's a popular small place that fills on long weekends, so book ahead and confirm your check-in time with the owner, especially for late arrivals.
pros: Consistently high reviews ~9+ · about 150 reviews
Shortcut to the walking street and riverside morning market
Kind owner, spotless rooms, balconies over the lotus pond
Breakfast included · free private parking · shared lounge/kitchen
cons: Small homestay, no 24-hour staff · no pool
Few rooms; fills fast on long weekends, book ahead

entries.name: TJ Boutique Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Wongsa Roj Rd · town centre · near the town market

entries.addr: 96/7 Wongsa Roj Rd, Uthai Mai, Mueang Uthai Thani
entries.storyHtml: TJ Boutique Hotel & Residence is a small in-town boutique run by the owner, praised for cleanliness and care that punches above its price, scoring about 8.4–8.6 from around 150 reviews and ranking among the top small stays in town on TripAdvisor. It's on Wongsa Roj Road, a walk from the town market. Real guest reviews praise an owner and staff who sweat the details — from restaurant and sightseeing tips to fruit left in the room — air-conditioned rooms with private balconies, free parking, and free bikes to ride along the Sakae Krang. But it's a small boutique with limited rooms, so book ahead, and there's no other meal service or pool. Best for a quiet, warm stay right in town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Book ahead, especially on long weekends, as rooms are limited. Borrow the hotel's bikes and ride along the Sakae Krang in the morning or evening. If you have dietary needs at breakfast, let them know in advance — it's served to your room.
pros: Owner-run and attentive · reviews especially praise cleanliness
In-town location, a walk from the town market
Rooms with private balconies · free parking · free bikes
Breakfast served to your room, dietary needs accommodated
cons: Small boutique, limited rooms; fills fast on long weekends
No other meal service or pool on site

entries.name: Sakaekrang Haven Homestay
entries.badge: 🌊 On the Sakae Krang · newly opened
entries.mrtTag: 📍 On the Sakae Krang · in town · ~2 km to the centre
tags: 🌊 Small garden cabins on the Sakae Krang
✨ New, clean rooms with garden/river-view balconies
entries.storyHtml: Sakaekrang Haven Homestay is a newly opened riverside homestay on the Sakae Krang that's earned high review scores around 9.0 from the start. It's a handful of small cabins in a riverside garden, in town about 2 km from the centre. Real guest reviews praise the new, clean, modern rooms, all with garden- or river-view balconies, a warm owner who runs it personally, a tasty Asian breakfast, and free parking. It is a new property, though — review numbers are still low — cabins are limited so book ahead, and there's no other meal service or pool on site. Best for sleeping by the river in town in a quiet, warm way.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a river-facing cabin if one's free, since the Sakae Krang view is the highlight. Walk or cycle along the river to the morning market early. Book ahead, especially on long weekends, and message your arrival time if you'll be late, as it's a small place.
pros: High reviews ~9.0 · on the Sakae Krang, quiet
New, clean, modern rooms with garden/river-view balconies
Owner-run and warm · tasty Asian breakfast
Free private parking · in town, short drives to temples & market
cons: Newly opened, few reviews · limited cabins, book ahead

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate from-rates for standard rooms outside peak season and can change by date and season; always check live prices and compare 3 sites before booking. Scores and standouts here come from reading real guest reviews on the booking platforms, not from personal stays. Every stay in this guide scores 8.1+, but these are budget 2–3 star properties, so they carry price-appropriate limits: nearly all have no pool (only Uthaithani Resort does), some are suburban or riverside and need a car with a drive into town for every meal, and some guesthouses have few rooms that fill fast — please read each one's caveats before booking. Most stays can be compared across all 3 sites, except Numhom Resort, whose third channel is Hotels.com rather than Booking.com. In the cool season and on long weekends, when tourists and cyclists flock to Uthai Thani, rates rise and small low-room-count stays sell out, so book ahead. Uthai Thani has no metro; riverside, Koh Thepho and suburban stays are far easier with a private car, while old-town stays are walkable. Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about budget Uthai Thani hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which budget Uthai Thani stay is the best value?
faq.a: By value (score for the price), Numhom Resort from ฿650, scoring 9.1 from 167 reviews, is the best value in this guide — the cheapest, yet almost the top score. Next come S Ville Resort ฿700 (big rooms with a bathtub) and C2U Hotel ฿800 (new clean rooms, the most reviews at 828). The highest scores in the guide are Numhom and Sabua The Terrace, both at 9.1.

faq.q: ❓ How much do budget Uthai Thani hotels cost?
faq.a: In this guide, prices start around ฿650–1,200/night. The cheapest are Numhom Resort ฿650, S Ville Resort ฿700, C2U Hotel ฿800 and Uthaithani Resort ฿850; the riverside/boutique stays are Ban Klang Gaew and Shon Boutique ฿900, Comenietee Uthai and TJ Boutique ฿1,000, and Sabua The Terrace and Sakaekrang Haven ฿1,200. All are approximate from-rates for standard rooms outside peak season; rates rise clearly in the cool season and on long weekends.

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in on a budget in Uthai Thani?
faq.a: It depends on your trip. The old town (Uthai Mai) suits those who want to wander, with the riverside morning market, the walking street and restaurants within walking distance (Comenietee Uthai, Sabua The Terrace, TJ Boutique, Shon Boutique). The Sakae Krang riverside and Koh Thepho suit those who want to sleep by the water and cycle (Sakaekrang Haven, Ban Klang Gaew). The suburbs toward Ban Rai (Tha Pho, Thap Than, Highway 333) suit drivers wanting a pool resort or a big room for less (Numhom Resort, Uthaithani Resort, C2U, S Ville).

faq.q: ❓ Is there a budget Uthai Thani hotel with a pool?
faq.a: Yes, but only one in this guide: Uthaithani Resort ฿850, with separate adult and kids' pools, family-friendly. The cheaper stays here (guesthouses, homestays, bungalows and small boutiques) mostly have no pool, leaning on location and atmosphere instead. If you need a pool on a budget, Uthaithani Resort is the best-value answer.

faq.q: ❓ Do I need a car for a budget Uthai Thani trip?
faq.a: Uthai Thani has no metro and is a small, flat town. Without a car, stay in the old town, walkable to the morning market, walking street and restaurants (Comenietee Uthai, Sabua The Terrace, TJ Boutique) — small enough to explore on foot or by bike. But riverside, Koh Thepho and suburban stays (Ban Klang Gaew, Sakaekrang Haven, Numhom, Uthaithani, C2U, S Ville) almost all need a car, as there's nothing walkable nearby — don't pick on price alone and get stuck without transport.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking Uthai Thani hotels?
faq.a: Prices differ across Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com depending on each site's promotions, so open and compare all three before booking — most stays in this guide compare across all 3 (Numhom Resort's third channel is Hotels.com rather than Booking.com). Every review page includes the comparison links. It can save hundreds of baht a night, especially for popular low-room-count stays in the cool season and on long weekends.
